approachQuestion.prompt: Many range totals on a fixed array. Return one sum for each inclusive query [left,right]. The immutable array has n values (1 <= n <= 100,000), and there are q queries (10,000 <= q <= 100,000); endpoints are valid and each answer fits in signed 64-bit. Example: values=[2,5,-1,4], queries=[[0,2],[1,3],[2,2]] returns [6,8,-1]. Choose a method for the stated large query workload.
constraints: All queries use the same unchanged array.
The output contains q sums and is excluded from auxiliary-space accounting.
Input is read-only; every prefix sum, not only requested answers, fits signed 64-bit; addition is constant time.

options.text: Make cumulative totals once, then answer each range by subtracting two stored totals (with a zero before the first element).
options.feedback: The one-time summary is reused by every query, and subtraction handles both endpoints consistently.

options.text: For every query, add all entries between its endpoints from the original array.
options.feedback: This is correct but repeats work; with n=q=100,000 and full-length ranges it visits about ten billion entries.

options.text: Store cumulative totals starting at index zero, then always subtract prefix[left] from prefix[right].
options.feedback: It omits values[left]. For values=[2,5,-1,4] and query [1,3], it returns 3 instead of 8.

options.text: Sort the values first, then build cumulative totals and use the original endpoints.
options.feedback: For values=[2,5,-1,4] and range [1,3], sorting gives [-1,2,4,5], whose positions 1..3 sum to 11 rather than the original range sum 8.

feedback.reason: A summary pays off when many queries reuse the same unchanged input.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for prefix-sums-for-many-ranges. The q returned sums are output and excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: n is the array length and q is the query count.
The cumulative table has one entry per input position plus a leading zero.

options.text: O(n + q) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: The cumulative table is built in one pass, then each query takes constant work. The table remains live and has linear size; the output array is excluded.

methodReveal.title: Reuse cumulative totals
methodReveal.description: Build prefix[0]=0 and prefix[i+1]=prefix[i]+values[i]. For each inclusive range, return prefix[right+1]-prefix[left]. The extra leading zero makes ranges beginning at index zero use the same formula.
